facts.text: Kew Gardens Hills is a residential neighborhood in central Queens, bounded by Union Turnpike, the Van Wyck Expressway, and Parsons Boulevard.
The neighborhood developed rapidly after World War II as returning veterans and their families sought affordable housing in the outer boroughs.
Kew Gardens Hills has a sizable Orthodox Jewish community and is home to several synagogues and Jewish day schools.
The Grand Central Parkway runs along the northern edge of the neighborhood, one of the main highways linking central Queens to JFK Airport.
Queens College, part of the City University of New York, is located just to the north in Flushing and draws many students who live in Kew Gardens Hills.
The name distinguishes this neighborhood from adjacent Kew Gardens, which lies to the west and is known for its proximity to Queens Borough Hall.
